headline: Bank of England: global AI debt issuance already more than double 2025's total
body: The Bank of England's Financial Policy Committee said on September 30 that Morgan Stanley estimated global AI-related debt issuance at around $450 billion as of early September, more than double the total issuance in all of 2025. JP Morgan analysts estimated AI-related capital expenditure financed through debt issuance could total around $4.1 trillion between 2026 and 2030. The FPC said this debt issuance broadens the exposure of capital markets to developments in AI.
note: The FPC warned that a reassessment of AI earnings expectations could affect AI-related asset valuations and sovereign debt markets at the same time, so the risk from AI-linked credit runs beyond any single lender into the funding markets banks and insurers both depend on.

evidence.text: Record of the Financial Policy Committee meeting on 25 September 2026
The rapid increase in artificial intelligence (AI)-related debt issuance broadens the exposure of capital markets to developments in AI.
As of early September, Morgan Stanley estimated that global AI-related debt issuance totalled around $450 billion, more than double the total issuance in all of 2025.
JP Morgan analysts estimated that AI-related capital expenditure financed through debt issuance would total around $4.1 trillion between 2026 and 2030.
A reassessment of those expectations could therefore affect not only AI-related asset valuations but also sovereign debt markets.
